result.title: What We Talk About When We Talk About Emotion Editing
result.summary: Emotional image editing aims to change the emotion a scene conveys while preserving its essential content. Because the same scene can support different emotional interpretations, achieving an emotional goal requires visual changes grounded in the source context. Motivated by the Component Process Model, which links emotional responses to event appraisal, we investigate neural representations as a reference for these editing decisions. Using TRIBE v2, an fMRI encoding model, we analyze 400 source-target pairs across eight emotion categories. Hidden states from EmoEdit, EmoEditor, and AffectDelta correspond more strongly to predicted target-image responses in visual regions than in affect-related regions. This imbalance motivates ROI-ReFT, which combines source visual responses as a content reference with a predicted affective response change as an editing direction. Two interacting branches use both conditions to guide a frozen editor throughout generation. Predicted responses of the generated image supervise affective change and constrain visual drift. On a post hoc selected subset of 400 editing requests, ROI-ReFT achieves 91.75% target-emotion accuracy and 83.25% joint success, with the same output both matching the target emotion and reaching source-output DINO-I of at least 0.80. Our code and dataset will be publicly released.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究情感图像编辑：用 fMRI 编码模型 TRIBE v2 分析三种编辑器的隐状态与预测脑区响应的对应关系，发现视觉区匹配强于情感区，据此提出 ROI-ReFT，以源图视觉响应为内容参照、预测情感响应变化为编辑方向，双分支引导冻结编辑器生成，并用生成图的预测响应监督情感变化、约束视觉漂移。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以预测 ROI 响应作表征层监督、并把「内容参照」与「变化方向」分离的条件引导方式，可能为 LVR 中锚定视觉证据、抑制状态漂移与信息坍缩提供可核查线索；但研究对象是图像编辑而非推理，视为方法借鉴需较多迁移核查。
